title: Source verification in Phase 4 Part 4
summary: The nine sources still pending were looked up again on 19 October 2026. Now checked: Peterson 2011 (abstract, PEDro record), Fragala 2019 (full text, NSCA), FDA General Wellness 2026 and MDCG 2019-11 rev.1 (primary texts), ADA Standards 2026 section 5 (official recommendation summary). Partly checked: LeSuer 1997 (part of the abstract) and the WHO waist protocol (through a paper using it). Still not opened: ACOG CO 804 and Campbell 2019 full texts (the publisher and PubMed/PMC refused the requests), GINA 2026's exercise section (the PDF text stops at page 31; the app's asthma entry doesn't rely on GINA). No rule's wording, parameters or confidence changes; only evidence records and verification notes do. The health-condition table (ADA, ACOG, Campbell) is versioned separately; its notes are listed in the Part 4 report.

approval.by: Delegated: evidence verification only (no wording, parameter or confidence change), reported to the Product Owner at the Phase 4 gate

Peterson2011.verification: checked 2026-10-19 (abstract, PEDro record 28020): 49 studies, 1,328 adults aged 50+; resistance exercise raised lean body mass by 1.1 kg (95% CI 0.9-1.2); higher-volume programmes gained more (beta 0.05), older age less (beta -0.03); I2 84%

Fragala2019.verification: checked 2026-10-19 (full text, NSCA PDF): 2-3 non-consecutive days a week per muscle group; working towards 2-3 sets of 1-2 multi-joint exercises per major muscle group at 70-85% 1RM (1 set and lighter loads to start for beginners and frail adults); power exercises fast in the lifting phase at 40-60% 1RM; multicomponent training (resistance, gait, balance) for older adults; frail adults may start at 20-30% 1RM

LeSuer1997.verification: partly checked 2026-10-19 (part of the abstract, Semantic Scholar): 67 untrained college students (40 men, 27 women); all correlations between predicted and achieved 1RM high (r > 0.95); the lift-by-lift accuracy part could not be read

WHOSTEPS.verification: partly checked 2026-10-19 through Statistics Canada Health Reports 2012 (82-003-X 2012003, article 11707), which uses the WHO protocol: the midpoint between the lowest rib and the top of the iliac crest, at the end of a normal breath out, and notes the WHO and NIH sites give different readings; the WHO 2011 report's PDF (iris.who.int) could not be read
WHOSTEPS.note: Primary source still to read: WHO. Waist circumference and waist-hip ratio: report of a WHO expert consultation, Geneva, 8-11 December 2008. WHO, 2011. ISBN 9789241501491.

ACOG20.verification: located; citation checked 2026-10-12 in Crossref; the full text could not be opened on 2026-10-12 or 2026-10-19 (acog.org and the publisher refused the request). A secondary summary of ACOG's earlier (2015) opinion lists broadly the same contraindications and warning signs; the 2020 details the app uses (placenta praevia after 28 weeks, growth restriction, triplets or more) still rest on the unread 2020 text

CAM19.verification: checked (abstract); full text not opened on 2026-10-19 (PubMed/PMC refused the request). The International Bone Metastases Exercise Working Group's 2022 recommendations (Campbell et al.; UBC summary) agree with the app's caution for bone spread: risk assessment and medical consultation before exercise, qualified supervision, lesion location considered

FDA26.citation: U.S. Food and Drug Administration. General Wellness: Policy for Low Risk Devices. Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff, 6 January 2026 (supersedes 27 September 2019).
FDA26.verification: checked 2026-10-19 (primary text): general wellness = intended only for general wellness use and low risk; claims such as logging, tracking or trending exercise and 'may help reduce the risk of' / 'may help living well with' a chronic condition are in scope; products whose labelling, user interface or functionality references specific diseases, clinical conditions or diagnostic thresholds are not general wellness products; a prompt to see a health professional is acceptable without thresholds, diagnoses or treatment advice

MDCG19-11.citation: Medical Device Coordination Group. MDCG 2019-11 rev.1: Qualification and classification of software - Regulation (EU) 2017/745 and Regulation (EU) 2017/746. June 2025.
MDCG19-11.verification: checked 2026-10-19 (primary text): software must have a medical purpose on its own to be a medical device; wellness or fitness apps do not qualify; the manufacturer's stated intended purpose decides qualification and class

changed_rules.reason: Fragala 2019 checked in full text (2-3 non-consecutive strength days; power at 40-60% 1RM; multicomponent training for older adults) and Peterson 2011 in abstract (+1.1 kg lean mass at 50+, more with higher volume): both agree with the rule
WHO waist protocol checked through a paper that uses it (midpoint of the lowest rib and the iliac crest, end of a normal breath out); the WHO 2011 report itself still to read
LeSuer 1997 abstract partly read (67 untrained students; predicted and achieved 1RM correlated r > 0.95); the lift-by-lift results still to read
